name: Fintech & Financial Services
label: SECTOR EXPLORATION PACK | WORKSHOP 1
referenceMarket: United States (Miami/Florida as a reference case; national-scope ideas are welcome)
intro: This Pack gives you a common starting point: vocabulary, structure and verified figures. It does not define the problem, customer or solution. That is your job.
definition: Businesses that move, store, lend, insure and manage money for consumers and companies, plus the technology and infrastructure that power them.
inside: Payments and money transfer, domestic and cross-border
Small business finance and B2B payments
Infrastructure: banking-as-a-service, compliance, fraud and data APIs. Secondary VC markets
outside: Crypto trading and token issuance as the core idea (payments or infrastructure that use blockchain can fit)
Bank branch operations and real estate

bank regulators (OCC, FDIC, Federal Reserve) and bank partnerships
boundaryRows.note: Know the rules that touch your idea; do not assume they block or enable it.

players.howMoney: Per-transaction fees (a percentage plus a fixed amount), network fees, software and hardware for merchants.
Interchange, subscription tiers, interest on loans, merchant fees (buy now pay later). Often rely on partner banks.
Transfer fee plus FX spread on each transaction; take rate on volume.

players.type: Small business finance and B2B payments
players.howMoney: SaaS subscription, interchange on corporate cards, interest, invoice-financing fees.
Premiums, agent commissions, managing-general-agent fees; claims cost drives profitability.
Fees on assets under management, subscriptions, interest on cash balances, payment for order flow.
API usage fees, SaaS per client, revenue share with banks. Covers data connectivity, card issuing, identity and fraud.

playersNote: Illustrative map, not exhaustive. Examples are well-known players to help you recognize each model, not a recommendation to copy them.

valueChain.note: One possible lens. The chain changes by segment (consumer banking, payments, lending, insurance, B2B infrastructure). Map the one that fits your area of interest and decide where value is created and captured.

figuresNote: Some figures are preliminary or estimates. Always check the latest release and cite the source and year in your own work.
challenge: Money touches every household and business, yet many consumers and small companies still face costly, slow or hard-to-access financial services, while banks, fintechs and infrastructure providers compete to serve them. Identify one specific, evidence-backed friction experienced by a clearly defined customer (a consumer, a small business or a financial institution), and show why it is worth solving now. Choose an initial launch market (for example Miami/Florida or another U.S. region) and justify your choice with data. Note how regulation affects your idea at seed stage.
pestelNote: Sprint 1, PESTEL: each team member takes one dimension. The figures above are a starting point only; look for what is changing and who it affects.

sprint2Questions.question: Which types of players hold the customer relationship and the license? Who depends on whom (banks, processors, partners)?
At which step of the money journey do customers pay too much, wait too long or drop out? Who captures the margin?
What do people or businesses still do manually, or avoid altogether? What evidence shows it matters (surveys, fees, rejection rates)?
How is the problem solved today, and by whom? Where do incumbents and fintechs fall short for this customer?
Which customer is most underserved: households, freelancers, small businesses, Hispanic and immigrant communities, cross-border senders? How large is it?
How does your idea make money (spread, fees, subscription, SaaS)? What are the unit economics and the regulatory cost of serving one customer?

glossary.def: Fee on each card payment, paid to the card issuer

Identity and anti-money-laundering checks required of financial firms

Banking-as-a-service: banks offer their license and rails via APIs

Share of a transaction a platform keeps as revenue
